Issued at 211 PM CST Fri Nov 20 2026

Currently...

A phrase said many times in this area...if it wasn't for that
wind it'd be a nice day. Started things off with plenty of 
cloud cover across the forecast area...satellite imagery showing
coverage diminishing over the past few hours, a trend expected 
to continue. Looking aloft...upper air and satellite data 
showing continued southwesterly across the Central Plains, set 
up between high pressure over central/northern portions of the 
East Coast and troughing extending from low pressure over the 
western half of Canada into central CA. Embedded in this trough 
are a couple smaller disturbances, one working ENE through WY, 
another sinking south through central CA. At the surface, the 
gusty winds that had already started ramping up last night as 
continued on into today...driven by a tighter pressure gradient 
between high pressure over much of the eastern CONUS and 
deepening low pressure/frontal boundary draped from eastern CO 
northward into the Dakotas. SSWrly winds with sustained speeds 
in the 25-30 MPH range continue, with gusts mainly in the 35-45 
MPH range. High temperatures remain on track top out in the mid-
upper 60s for most spots. 

Tonight through the weekend...

This evening into tonight...as the upper level
troughing/disturbances continue to shift east, the 
accompanying surface cold front will do the same. Not a lot of 
change with the general timing, moving into far NWrn areas early
this evening, making it roughly halfway through the area by 
sunrise Saturday. A handful of models continue to show the 
potential for at least some isolated precip or even just 
sprinkles accompanying that frontal boundary...so kept a low-end
chance (20 percent) across the NW this evening, then a mention 
of isolated sprinkles through much of the overnight period. The 
front starting to work through tonight could make for quite a 
range in low temperatures...currently have mid-30s in the far NW
to low-mid 50s in the SE. 

For Saturday into Saturday night...main story lies with the 
continued progress of this frontal boundary and increasing 
preciptiation chances. Overall hasn't been any notable changes
with models...which show the main trough axis by evening time 
emerging onto the High Plains (with more organized lows over the
US/Can border and the eastern CO/NM border). Through the 
overnight hours- early Sun AM...the axis continues east and 
looks to be just off to the east of the forecast area. Main 
chances for precipitation will remain generally along the 
accompany lower level frontal boundary...likely more isolated in
nature through the morning hours, increasing in coverage 
through the afternoon as the better upper level forcing arrives.
Model agreement continues to focus on the best chances being 
roughly along/east of a York NE-Osborne KS line, closer to the 
lower level front...but can't rule out scattered activity a bit 
further NW tied closer to the mid-upper level trough axis. 
Activity is expected taper off late evening, forecast is dry 
after 09Z. Not expecting notable rain totals...with 
probabilities of 0.1in or more exceeding 60 percent only across 
our far SErn areas, and only around a 10 percent chance of 
0.5in. The surface cold front ushers in a switch to northerly 
winds, but models aren't showing a push of significantly 
stronger winds, speeds mainly top out around 15-20 MPH. There is
a better push of cooler air...and highs for Saturday remain 
trick due to the daytime frontal passage and increasing precip 
chances...current forecast ranges from the mid 40s NW to low 60s
SE. 

Forecast for Sunday remains dry...as the Plains sit in more 
zonal/progressive upper level flow in the wake of Saturday's
system. Expecting more sun...with winds tapering off from west
to east...but the cooler temps spread area-wide, forecast to 
top out in the upper 30s to mid 40s. Normal for this time of 
year is mid 40s-near 50.

New work week/Thanksgiving...

No notable changes in the forecast to start off the work
week...with models keeping things dry for Monday. With time, 
the upper level pattern turns more southwesterly in nature, as 
another shortwave disturbance is making its way east across the 
Rockies. The lighter winds on Sunday turn back to the SSE for 
Monday as sfc low pressure deepens over eastern CO, but not 
expecting notable increases in speed, generally around 10-15 MPH
(perhaps some higher gusts across western areas). High 
temperatures are similar to Sunday, topping out in the upper 
30s-mid 40s.

Monday night into Tuesday brings the only precipitation chances 
currently in the forecast for the Mon-Wed timeframe...and they 
are not great chances. Still some differences with the strength 
of the system, but agreement isn't too bad at this point that 
the better chances are not much better than a glancing blow
